title: Fri 20 Nov · morning check
summary:
[b]Overnight:[/b] Japan core CPI 2.2% vs 2.3% expected (yen shadow −2 → EURJPY, CHFJPY, CADJPY turn two-sided, GBPJPY and NZDJPY lean bullish); Wall Street −2% and VIX closed ~28.4 (franc trigger met on a close); December Fed hike still ~96%.
[b]Next (Bucharest):[/b] UK retail sales 09:00, Lagarde 10:30, Waller 15:25, Canada retail sales 15:30, US Michigan 17:00, Cook 19:15; Friday closes set the W48 risk regime.

USD.note: Stocks fell 2% but December hike odds held near 96%; Barr: inflation too high.

EUR.note: No spread print after 156.3bp (17 Nov); Senate budget (PLF) debate opens today.

GBP.note: No BoE item overnight; UK retail sales at 09:00 are the next test.

JPY.note: Core CPI 2.2% vs 2.3% expected (second soft surprise after GDP): shadow −2; 0 if read as in line.

CHF.note: VIX closed about 28.4: the franc condition is met on a close; score re-measured from Friday closes.

CAD.note: No Canadian item overnight; retail sales at 15:30 Bucharest.

AUD.note: Jobs-miss condition still met; shadow +3 central, 0 if the RBA outlook (R2) is cut.

NZD.note: No New Zealand item overnight; most exposed to a −2 risk regime at Friday close.

XAU.note: Gold factor −3 unchanged (spot near $3,675); XAU shadow +3 only via the USD shadow.

[b]Tokyo's inflation came in a touch cooler than hoped, and the yen lost another piece of its story.[/b]
Core consumer prices rose 2.2% in October, faster than September's 2.1% but below the 2.3% economists had pencilled in. After Monday's GDP miss, that is the second top-tier Japanese release this week to undershoot. The surprise score now sums to −2, which pulls the yen's shadow to −2. Analysts still expect a BoJ hike on 18 December, so this is a nudge, not a collapse.
